_comment: Country risk bands, cargo profiles and cover definitions used by the risk assessment stage. Edit this file to update the exercise — no code changes needed.

coverFloor._comment: Underwriting policy, not law. Nothing in the Institute Cargo Clauses, the Incoterms or any transport convention sets a minimum cover for a commodity. This is TTCircle refusing to write ICC (C) over cargo that is exposed to the two perils ICC (C) does not reach. Edit the list to change the policy; the score itself is untouched.
coverFloor.recommendation: ICC (B) — raised from ICC (C). This cargo is exposed to theft and to water damage, and ICC (C) reaches neither.
coverFloor.label: Why the recommendation was raised
coverFloor.note: The score for this shipment came out low enough for ICC (C). TTCircle does not write ICC (C) over this cargo: condensation in a container and pilferage of finished goods are the two most common causes of loss here, and ICC (C) covers major casualties only.
coverFloor.caveat: This is TTCircle’s underwriting judgement, not a rule. No clause or convention sets a minimum cover for a commodity. The binding minimums come from elsewhere: the Incoterm agreed — CIF A5 requires ICC (C) as a minimum, CIP A5 requires ICC (A) — and whatever a letter of credit or the sales contract stipulates. Know which of the three you are looking at before you argue about it.

scoreLimits.title: What this score does not include
scoreLimits.body: This assessment uses six fields. It does not know your routing detail or whether the service tranships, your delivery deadline, the terms of your sales contract, your buyer’s quality protocol, the condition of the goods when they were loaded, or the season you are shipping in.
scoreLimits.closing: A risk assessment tells you what kind of shipment this is. It does not tell you what is wrong with yours.

recommendations.text: ICC (C) — minimal coverage is sufficient for this low-risk shipment.
ICC (B) — basic coverage recommended for moderate protection.
ICC (A) + carrier liability advised: the combination of route and cargo raises the exposure.
ICC (A) together with IWC and ISRCC extensions is strongly recommended for this high-risk scenario.

icca.reach: ICC (A) — all risks, subject to exclusions. Reaches theft, water damage and handling damage.
icca.name: ICC (A) — Comprehensive coverage
icca.text: Covers all risks of loss or damage to the cargo except the listed exclusions (war and strikes unless separately added, inherent vice, insufficient packing, wilful misconduct). The right choice for high-value or sensitive shipments.

iccb.reach: ICC (B) — major casualties plus water damage. Does not reach theft.
iccb.name: ICC (B) — Basic cargo coverage
iccb.text: Covers named perils: fire, explosion, stranding, sinking, collision, general average, jettison, water entering the vessel or container. Excludes theft, pilferage and most handling damage.

iccc.reach: ICC (C) — major casualties only. No theft, no water damage.
iccc.name: ICC (C) — Minimal cargo coverage
iccc.text: Covers major catastrophes only: fire, explosion, stranding, sinking, overturning, collision and general average sacrifice. Suitable for low-value, robust cargo on stable routes.

iwc.name: IWC — Institute War Clauses
iwc.text: Covers loss caused by war, civil war, hostilities, capture, seizure, derelict mines and torpedoes. Normally added on top of ICC (A) when the route crosses a listed high-risk area.

isrcc.name: ISRCC — Strikes, Riots and Civil Commotion
isrcc.text: Covers loss caused by strikers, locked-out workers, labour disturbances, riots, civil commotions and acts of terrorism. Recommended for volatile regions and for cargo dwelling in port.
